case_title: Atul Thakur v. State of Himachal Pradesh etc.
accused_victim_relationship: Acquaintance (friends who had gathered for a drink party; trial court noted cordial relations and no enmity, as quoted by the Supreme Court)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.201 read with s.34 (charged); s.304 Part II (conviction finally upheld)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PW-11, PW-12); recovery of knife at accused's instance; nature of injuries attributed to the knife; telephone call corroborated by PW-2 (father)
aggravating_circumstances: Six knife blows on different parts of body; use of knife; victim unarmed (relied on by High Court, held not decisive by Supreme Court)
mitigating_circumstances: Sudden fight in heat of passion; no premeditation; no intention to cause death; offered water and took victim to hospital; stayed until last rites
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.304 Part II IPC; rigorous imprisonment 5 years and fine Rs.10,000, default 1 year further RI
high_court_outcome: Appeal against conviction dismissed on facts; conviction altered to s.302 IPC (life imprisonment with fine); co-accused acquittal affirmed
offence_finally_established: IPC s.304 Part II (culpable homicide not amounting to murder)
neutral_facts: On a night in late July 2011, a group of friends gathered at a house for a drink party arranged at the behest of the victim, a 22-year-old man. During the gathering the victim, while smoking, blew smoke into the face of the accused. The accused objected that the victim was junior in age and should not smoke in the accused's presence. A sudden physical fight followed, and the accused struck the victim with a knife six times on different parts of the body. Two friends who were present as eyewitnesses testified that, after realising the victim was badly injured, the accused offered water and took the victim to hospital with other friends. The accused stayed at the hospital until the victim died. The accused also telephoned the victim's father and asked him to come to the hospital. Eyewitnesses stated that doctors did not give immediate treatment but insisted on first calling the father. Police received a telephone message about a quarrel near a tunnel and an injured person being taken to hospital. The Station House Officer recorded the statement of the victim's father under section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The knife was recovered at the accused's instance, and the nature of the injuries was attributed to the same knife. Four persons who had gathered at the house were proceeded against, and three of them were later separated from the case. The victim died from the knife injuries.
offence_severity: Not stated (judgment records only the respondents' submission that s.302 carries life imprisonment)
physical_harm: Six knife wounds on different parts of the body; victim died
number_of_offences: 2 charged (s.302; s.201 read with s.34); 1 finally upheld (s.304 Part II)
premeditation_planning: No premeditation or planning found; act was sudden and in heat of passion
motive: Sudden quarrel after victim blew cigarette smoke into accused's face (accepted by the Supreme Court as the trigger; trial court had found no proven motive)
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of PW-11 and PW-12 on sudden fight and aftermath; recovery of knife at accused's instance; nature of injuries matching the knife; PW-2 corroboration of the telephone call
witness_credibility: Eyewitnesses PW-11 and PW-12 found reliable and present throughout; concurrent findings on their evidence upheld; PW-2 corroborates the telephone call
post_offence_conduct: Offered water, took victim to hospital, stayed there, and telephoned the victim's father to come to the hospital
custody_duration: Per appellant's counsel: 7 years 3 months 24 days served as on 24 November 2017, including remission of 1 year 2 months 6 days
trial_duration: offence: 27.07.2011 (night of incident; telephone message 28.07.2011); trial judgment: 31.12.2014; High Court: 01.04.2016; Supreme Court: 19.01.2018
legal_representation: Accused: Aditya Dhawan, Ms. Kiran Dhawan, Chander Shekhar Ashri. State/respondents: D. K. Thakur (AAG), Shariq Ahmed, Ms. Taiba Khan, Ajay Marwah
investigation_status: FIR-equivalent statement recorded under s.154 CrPC; investigation completed; four persons sent for trial
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted s.304 Part II, 5 years RI and Rs.10,000 fine. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction altered to s.302 (life with fine). Supreme Court: partly allowed; s.304 Part II with 10 years RI and Rs.10,000 fine
prosecution_argument: Guilt supported by evidence; High Court rightly held the offence to be murder under s.302 given the repeated knife blows; appeals devoid of merit
defence_argument: Contradictions in eyewitness evidence; genesis of offence doubtful; involvement not proved beyond reasonable doubt; at best Exception 4 to s.300 (s.304 Part II); sentence already undergone
legal_principle_applied: Exception 4 to s.300 IPC: sudden fight, heat of passion, no premeditation, no undue advantage or cruel manner; number of wounds and use of knife not decisive; court must take an overall view
precedent_relied_upon: Surain Singh v. State of Punjab (2017) 5 SCC 796
sentencing_rationale: Trial court's five-year sentence gave no special reasons; nature of offence, trivial reason for anger, knife use and multiple blows do not warrant light punishment; 10 years with fine meets the ends of justice
judicial_mitigating_factors: Sudden fight; heat of passion; no premeditation; no undue advantage or cruel manner; no intention to cause death
judicial_aggravating_factors: Nature of offence; trivial reason for anger; use of knife; multiple blows
other_sentence_order: Entitled to set off under s.428 CrPC
